speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Gastroenteritis typically does not cause a spinning sensation; given your severe vertigo, nausea, and vomiting, let's explore if you experienced any recent head trauma or if the dizziness is worse when you turn your head.

REQUEST TEST: Vestibular_Swab
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Internal_Auditory_Canals

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vestibular_Swab: NORMAL READINGS.; MRI_Internal_Auditory_Canals: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal MRI and vestibular swab rule out acoustic neuroma and labyrinthitis, so we need to determine if this is a central cause or a peripheral issue like BPPV. Has the spinning sensation been triggered specifically by changes in head position, such as rolling over in bed or looking up?

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike_Manual_Examination
REQUEST TEST: Gait_Assessment

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dix-Hallpike_Manual_Examination: Positive, inducing nystagmus and reproducing patient's symptoms of vertigo when head is turned to the left and laid back. Gait_Assessment: Normal, consistent with healthy man with a normal gait.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The positive Dix-Hallpike test with nystagmus upon left lateral positioning, combined with your normal gait and the absence of central signs on MRI, confirms BPPV. We can proceed with canalith repositioning maneuvers to treat this.
